dor.title: Division of Responsibility
dor.intro: Feeding goes best when parents and children each do their own jobs. Pressure, bribes and praise for eating usually make picky eating last longer.

parent.what: What food is offered, including one food your child usually eats.
parent.when: When meals and snacks happen, on a steady rhythm.
parent.where: Where food is eaten, ideally together at the table without screens.
parent.company: Making meals pleasant: calm talk, no comments on how much is eaten.

child.whether: Whether to eat what is offered.
child.howMuch: How much to eat, from what is on the table.

refuses.say: You don't have to eat it. The next food is at snack time.
refuses.avoid: Just one more bite, then you can go.

onlyWants.say: Rice is here, and there is chicken too. You can choose from what is on the table.
onlyWants.avoid: Fine, I'll make you something else.

reward.when: You want to offer a reward
reward.say: Dessert is part of dinner today, and it comes with the meal.
reward.avoid: Eat your vegetables and you get a sweet.

grazing.when: They ask for snacks all day
grazing.say: The kitchen is closed for now. Snack is at four, after Asr.
grazing.avoid: Here, take some chips so you stop asking.

newFood.when: A new food is on the table
newFood.say: This is spinach. It's a bit soft and a bit salty. You can look at it or pass it to me.
newFood.avoid: Just try it, you'll like it.

sweets.say: Sweets are with the meal today. Let's put one on your plate.
sweets.avoid: No sweets until you finish everything.

cleanPlate.say: Is your tummy full? Then you can say Alhamdulillah and go play.
cleanPlate.avoid: Finish your plate, there are children with nothing to eat.

sibling.say: Everyone eats in their own way and at their own pace.
sibling.avoid: Look at your sister, she ate it all.

dor.source: Based on Ellyn Satter's Division of Responsibility in Feeding. Draft content, pending review by the content team.
